local_entities.label: Tuvok as represented in Excelsior-era memory
Janeway as observer within Tuvok's mind-meld memory
Hikaru Sulu as represented in Tuvok's memory
Dimitri Valtane as represented in Tuvok's memory
Neurotropic viral parasite disguised as memory engram

evidence.summary: A present-day nebula triggers Tuvok's vivid image of a falling girl accompanied by strong emotion even though he says the event never happened to him.
The Doctor initially diagnoses t'lokan schism from apparent repressed memory disruption and warns that ongoing hippocampal damage may become fatal.
Janeway joins Tuvok in a mind-meld intending to observe a childhood memory but instead enters Tuvok's remembered service aboard the Excelsior during the Praxis shock wave and related events.
The memory presents young Tuvok objecting to Sulu's unauthorized rescue mission, revealing his early Starfleet dissatisfaction and relationship to regulations.
Voyager analysis finds the present nebula and Tuvok's remembered Excelsior nebula visually similar but technically distinct, weakening a simple physical causal link.
Repeated mind-meld attempts replay Excelsior events while the falling-girl image resurfaces around Valtane's remembered injury/death; Janeway and Tuvok become neurologically locked in the meld.
Thoron radiation exposes and destroys a viral parasite embedded in Tuvok's brain; the Doctor concludes it disguised itself as a memory engram, using the falling-girl image as camouflage.
The Doctor states the pathogen feeds on brain peptides and evades immunity by masquerading as remembered content rather than being an authentic repressed childhood memory.
Tuvok confirms portions of his Excelsior service history and reflects on those days without claiming nostalgia; Janeway says the shared mind-meld made her feel partly present in them.

assertions.subject: voy-fb:janeway_observer
counterevidence: Her presence in the memory does not make her an historical participant in Excelsior events.

assertions.subject: voy-fb:excelsior_memory
counterevidence: A memory environment is source-relative recollection rather than independent archival reconstruction of every historical detail.

neutral_coding.plot_problem: An apparent repressed memory threatens Tuvok neurologically and draws Janeway through memories of his Excelsior service before the cause is identified as a parasite.
neutral_coding.epistemics: Mind-meld memories, present medical readings, historical recollection, and pathogen-generated imagery remain separate evidence layers.
neutral_coding.identity_memory: Janeway is an observer in Tuvok's remembered environment, not retroactively an Excelsior crew member; the falling girl is a memory artifact rather than a recovered childhood person/event.
neutral_coding.counterevidence: Authentic Excelsior memories coexist with a false viral memory image, so discovering manipulation in one element does not invalidate the whole remembered sequence.
